biological.citation: Macrocephaly and developmental delay caused by missense variants in RAB5C (PMID: 37552066)
biological.summary: Twelve individuals with nine different heterozygous de novo RAB5C variants exhibited macrocephaly and developmental delay. In vitro biochemical studies showed variants increased nucleotide exchange rate and attenuated GEF responsivity. C. elegans studies confirmed variants caused endocytic pathway defects in vivo, with two variants acting through dominant negative mechanisms; expression of human RAB5C variants in zebrafish caused defective development.

biological.citation: Rab5c-mediated endocytic trafficking regulates hematopoietic stem and progenitor cell development via Notch and AKT signaling (PMID: 32275659)
biological.summary: Rab5c is essential for hematopoietic stem and progenitor cell (HSPC) specification in zebrafish by regulating endocytic trafficking of Notch ligands/receptor and AKT signaling. Rab5c interacts with Appl1 in endosomes to support hemogenic endothelium survival via AKT signaling. Both Rab5c deficiency and overactivation impair HSPC production through disruption of endolysosomal trafficking.

biological.citation: The endosomal RIN2/Rab5C machinery prevents VEGFR2 degradation to control gene expression and tip cell identity during angiogenesis (PMID: 33983539)
biological.summary: RIN2/Rab5C prevents lysosomal degradation of internalized VEGFR2 in human endothelial cells, sustaining VEGF signaling through ERK and PI3-K pathways. Knockdown and CRISPR/Cas9 editing of Rab5C disrupted VEGF target gene expression and tip/stalk cell specification. Live-cell imaging in zebrafish confirmed that endosomal stabilization of VEGFR2 by Rab5C is required for developmental angiogenesis in vivo.

biological.citation: RAB5c controls the assembly of non-canonical autophagy machinery to promote phagosome maturation and microbicidal function of macrophages (PMID: 40196584)
biological.summary: RAB5c is necessary for LC3-associated phagocytosis (LAP) in macrophages by regulating phagosome recruitment of PI(3)P- and ROS-generating complexes. RAB5c facilitates phagosome translocation of the V-ATPase transmembrane core, enabling ATG16L1 binding and LC3 conjugation to single membranes. RAB5c depletion impaired macrophage elimination of Aspergillus fumigatus, and disruption of the V-ATPase-ATG16L1 axis increased susceptibility in vivo.

biological.citation: RAB5C Increases Endothelial Release of VWF by Regulating Vesicle Trafficking (PMID: 41537263)
biological.summary: RAB5C regulates von Willebrand Factor (VWF) exocytosis from endothelial cells; silencing decreased VWF release while overexpression or constitutively active RAB5C increased it. Proximity labeling and mass spectrometry identified 147 proteins proximal to RAB5C, revealing SNAP29 (a SNARE-associated protein) as a key RAB5C interactor mediating VWF exocytosis. Two GWAS-identified variants (rs9915255 and rs9912088) were shown to regulate RAB5C expression in stem cell-derived endothelial cells.

biological.citation: Rab5 isoforms orchestrate a 'division of labor' in the endocytic network; Rab5C modulates Rac-mediated cell motility (PMID: 24587345)
biological.summary: Among the three Rab5 isoforms, only Rab5C silencing in HeLa and U937 cells reduced membrane ruffles, cell migration, and EGF-stimulated Rac1 activation. Rab5C depletion also suppressed EGF-stimulated Akt phosphorylation and reduced focal adhesion foci, linking Rab5C specifically to growth factor-driven Rac1 activation and directional cell motility. Rab5A and Rab5B silencing did not recapitulate these phenotypes, demonstrating isoform-specific function.

biological.citation: S100P is a ferroptosis suppressor to facilitate hepatocellular carcinoma development by rewiring lipid metabolism (PMID: 39779666)
biological.summary: RAB5C directs ACC1 (acetyl-CoA carboxylase alpha) to the lysosome via P62-dependent selective autophagy, mediating S100P-induced lysosomal degradation of ACC1 in HCC cells. Knockdown of RAB5C abrogated S100P-induced ACC1 degradation and restored ferroptotic sensitivity of HCC cells. This identifies RAB5C as a key component of an anti-ferroptosis pathway that rewires lipid metabolism in hepatocellular carcinoma.

biological.citation: Rab5c promotes RSV and ADV replication by autophagy in respiratory epithelial cells (PMID: 38242290)
biological.summary: Activated Rab5c promotes RSV and adenovirus replication in A549 cells and Rab5c-overexpressing mice, while inactivated Rab5c inhibits replication. The mechanism is autophagy-dependent rather than endocytosis-dependent: Rab5c upregulates LC3-II by interacting with Beclin1, inducing autophagy that facilitates viral replication. Rab5c is localized on cell membranes and early endosomes/phagosomes and participates in clathrin-mediated endocytosis and early endosome fusion.

biological.citation: Rab5C enhances resistance to ionizing radiation in rectal cancer (PMID: 30968159)
biological.summary: Rab5C protein expression was significantly increased in residual rectal adenocarcinoma tumor tissues after neoadjuvant chemoradiation compared to pre-treatment biopsies, alongside Ku70 and Ku80. In a radiotherapy-resistant rectal adenocarcinoma cell line, Rab5C modulated EGFR internalization and nuclear relocalization in response to irradiation, affecting DNA repair protein expression and cell resistance. These findings identify Rab5C as a potential target for sensitizing rectal cancer cells to radiotherapy.
biological.sample_size: Stage II/III rectal adenocarcinoma patients (biopsy pairs)

biological.citation: ASHG 2023 - Coronary artery disease-associated splicing variants in vascular smooth muscle cells (N. Perry et al.)
biological.summary: RAB5C was identified as one of six genes containing SNPs both within CAD GWAS loci and highly predicted to affect smooth muscle cell-specific alternative splicing events. Splicing quantitative trait loci (sQTL) for RAB5C colocalized with CAD risk associations in aortic smooth muscle cells from 151 heart transplant donors. Long-read PacBio sequencing confirmed the alternative splicing predictions, implicating RAB5C splicing regulation in CAD susceptibility.
biological.sample_size: 151 heart transplant donors; 6 donors for long-read sequencing
